chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Django as a baby who ignored money
summary: Briggs describes Django as childlike, skipping a packed Saturday to play for nothing in a Montmartre cafe.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what kind of a guy was Django?

He was so much a baby that he would wait on a Saturday night, when the place was packed and jammed, and not show up. He wouldn't show up, but he'd phoned and say, 'Art,' he said, 'I am having a good time.' You know where he's at --
In Montmartre, playing in a cafe for nothing. For nothing, just playing in a cafe, having a good time. That's all.
And he could have been down making some money --
Oh, money meant nothing to him.
